fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. Luke says Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there (Luke 19:45). The sellers were right there in the courts, and Jesus started driving them out.

Not quite, friend. The text says Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there (Luke 19:45). So He did find sellers, and He did start driving them out. I once got shoved to the back of a junk drawer, so I know a little about being moved along.

Yes, baker. Luke says they could not find a way to do so, "…because all the people hung on His words." (Luke 19:48). The leaders were intent on killing Him (Luke 19:47), but the crowd stuck close to every word Jesus said. So the leaders came up empty.

That's it, baker. They said, "Tell us, by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?" (Luke 20:2). That's two questions in one breath, a real double batch! They want to know the authority, and they want to know who gave it.

Good guess, friend, but that's not what they ask here. The chief priests, scribes and elders ask, "by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?" (Luke 20:2). Fasting never comes up in this passage.
Nice reach, friend, but Moses never shows up in this scene. Jesus asks, "John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?" (Luke 20:4). The question is about John's baptism, and that's where it stays.
Ooh, a throne, friend! Fancy guess, but Jesus asks about John's baptism. His words are, "John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?" (Luke 20:4). Nobody in this scene brings up David.
Priest sounds like a solid guess, friend, but it's not the word here. The text says "…they are convinced that John was a prophet." (Luke 20:6). The word that fits the blank is prophet.
Ooh, king, friend! That's a big title, but it's not the one in this verse. The text says "…they are convinced that John was a prophet." (Luke 20:6). The blank is prophet.
I see the thinking, friend, but the leaders say something much sharper. They say, "all the people will stone us…" (Luke 20:6). I think that's a lot heavier than just being tuned out.
Remember sounds smart, friend, but it's not the word. The text says they answered "…that they did not know where it was from." (Luke 20:7). The word that goes in the blank is know.
Not that one, friend. Luke says they answered "…that they did not know where it was from." (Luke 20:7). Care is a bold guess, but the word the text gives is know.

Not quite, friend. After the leaders answer that they did not know, Jesus replies, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things." (Luke 20:8). So He doesn't tell them where His authority comes from. Their answer was that they didn't know, and His was that He wouldn't tell.
